html:
The Épera are a small Indigenous people of the province of Esmeraldas in northwest Ecuador, on the rivers near the Colombian border. They speak a Chocoan language close to that of the Emberá of Colombia and Panama, and are part of the same people as the Eperara Siapidara.

They live in houses on stilts along the rivers, fishing, hunting and farming plantains. The Épera of Ecuador are thought to have come south from Colombia in the 1900s. Their neighbours include the Chachi and the Wounaan.
